findings.reason: Web/Program.cs calls UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization and then UseCoreSyncHttpServer with no RequireAuthorization, fallback policy or gating middleware, and the RequireSyncReadWrite policy is never used. In Entra mode a request with no token gets through anonymously. The change's own wash-coresync-auth.md admits the server 'does not reject unauthenticated requests', yet its Context says the sync channel needed protection.
findings.claim: The CoreSync sync server never requires authentication, even with Auth:UseEntraId=true, so anonymous or bad-token requests still reach the sync tables.
findings.evidence: Program.cs calls `app.UseAuthentication(); app.UseAuthorization();` and then `app.UseCoreSyncHttpServer();`. Nothing gates the request in between: no RequireAuthorization, no fallback policy, no middleware that checks `User.Identity.IsAuthenticated`. The `RequireSyncReadWrite` policy is registered at line 29 but nothing references it. Trace: with Entra on, a sync request with no Authorization header gets NoResult from the bearer handler, and a bad token gets Fail with no challenge. UseAuthorization has no endpoint metadata to check, so the request reaches UseCoreSyncHttpServer anonymously. The builder's own doc confirms it (.squad/decisions/inbox/wash-coresync-auth.md: "does not reject unauthenticated requests (no RequireAuthorization() on CoreSync middleware endpoints)"), even though its Context says "the sync channel needed the same protection". ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddSyncServices exposes UserProfile, Conversation, VocabularyProgress and other tables as UploadAndDownload. The comment at lines 48-50 ("in production, Bearer tokens are validated") implies enforcement that does not exist. The diff adds no test for the Web project.

findings.reason: GetValue<bool> defaults to false and the else branch always registers DevAuthHandler, with no IsDevelopment() guard; Web/Program.cs does the same. Lowered to medium because DevAuthHandler was always on before this change, so the exposure is not new, but the new switch fails open.
findings.claim: Auth fails open: when Auth:UseEntraId is missing or false, including in Production, DevAuthHandler authenticates every request as dev-user.
findings.evidence: `var useEntraId = builder.Configuration.GetValue<bool>("Auth:UseEntraId");` returns false when the key is absent. The else branch then registers `AddScheme<..., DevAuthHandler>` as the default scheme, and `DevAuthHandler.HandleAuthenticateAsync` always returns `AuthenticateResult.Success` with dev-user claims. Web/Program.cs:20-38 follows the same pattern. The flag is only set in appsettings.Development.json, which is not loaded outside Development. appsettings.json is gitignored (.gitignore:411), and AppHost sets `Auth__UseEntraId` to "false". Trace: with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production, an anonymous `POST /api/v1/ai/chat` passes `.RequireAuthorization()` and triggers a billed OpenAI call, and `POST /api/v1/vocabulary/{wordId}/status` writes progress as dev-user. Before this change DevAuthHandler was always on, so exposure is unchanged, not new. But the change presents the switch as "Ready for production" (wash-api-jwt-bearer.md) without refusing the Dev scheme outside IsDevelopment().

findings.reason: The diff adds .WithEnvironment("Auth__UseEntraId", "false") on api; environment variables take precedence over JSON config. The web resource gets no Auth__ or AzureAd__ values. Lowered to low: it is a configuration and drift problem, not a traced runtime defect today.
findings.claim: AppHost hard-codes Auth__UseEntraId=false on the API, which overrides appsettings, and passes no Auth/AzureAd settings to the Web sync server.
findings.evidence: `.WithEnvironment("Auth__UseEntraId", "false")` sits on the `api` resource. Environment variables take precedence over JSON files in the default ASP.NET configuration stack. Line 27, `var web = builder.AddProject<SentenceStudio_Web>("web");`, passes no Auth__ or AzureAd__ values, so outside Development the Web project has no AzureAd section. Setting UseEntraId=true there would fail Microsoft.Identity.Web configuration. The tenant and client IDs are also copied by hand into both appsettings.Development.json files, AppHost and the AppLib handler's scopes, so they can drift apart.

findings.reason: Program.cs:37-47 registers four scope policies, but the endpoints use a bare .RequireAuthorization() (e.g. line 108), and the dev branch at line 53 registers no policies. The decision doc says scope enforcement was left for later, so the scopes are not enforced.
findings.claim: No endpoint uses the scope policies, so any valid token for the API audience can reach every endpoint, AI and speech included; the policies also exist only in the Entra branch.

findings.reason: The middleware looks up only the short names 'tid' and 'oid', and TestJwtGenerator also adds tenant_id and NameIdentifier, so the test would pass even if those lookups failed. Whether Microsoft.Identity.Web 3.8.2 remaps these claims by default depends on library behaviour the repository does not settle.
findings.claim: With real Entra tokens, the default inbound claim mapping may rename tid/oid to long URI claim types, so TenantId comes out null and UserId falls back to sub; the test token hides this.
findings.evidence: The middleware only looks up the short names: `FindFirstValue("tid") ?? FindFirstValue("tenant_id")` and `FindFirstValue("oid") ?? FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)`. Real Entra access tokens carry no `tenant_id`, and NameIdentifier is mapped from `sub`. The token in TestJwtGenerator.GenerateToken (lines 37-42) carries `tenant_id` and `ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier` with the same values as `tid` and `oid`. So API_ExtractsTenantContext gets the expected TenantId and UserId through the DevAuth fallbacks even if the `tid`/`oid` lookups never match. The bootstrap endpoint (Program.cs:103-106) also falls back to the raw `tenant_id` and NameIdentifier claims.

findings.reason: The diff sets Email = FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.Email) ?? FindFirstValue("preferred_username"), so in Entra mode a non-email, unverified identifier can end up in TenantContext.Email.
findings.claim: Email falls back to preferred_username, which is mutable and need not be an email address.
findings.evidence: `mutableContext.Email = context.User.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.Email) ?? context.User.FindFirstValue("preferred_username");` Entra access tokens include `email` only when it is configured as an optional claim, so in Entra mode this fallback will usually be the one used. The same `preferred_username` is also a DisplayName fallback (line 33).
